text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Norway's largest electricity producer, state-owned Statkraft, says there is no real danger of an acute power shortage this winter. The "power-crisis" is created by media hysteria, Statkraft says. Statkraft spokesman Geir Fugleseth says there is enough water in the hydropower reservoirs. A power crisis could only result from a hard drought, he says.

-The investigation into the Russian airliner crash on the arctic island of Spitzbergen last week, has revealed that the Russian pilot did not know the plane was off course when the aircraft slammed into a mountainside.

-The government Statistics Bureau, in a quarterly report on key economic indicators, upgraded the annual 1997 inflation forcast to 2.2 percent from 2.0 percent in its forecast in June. Price growth was revised upward because of increasing electricity prices.

-The Oslo Bourse has transferred international software house Sysdeco Group ASA to its observations list following information from the Morgan Grenfell Asset Managment Ltd that the group may hold 51 percent of the Norwegian company. Under Norwegian securities regulations, a company is obliged to make an offer to the remaining shareholder once it has acquired 45 percent or more of the issued equity in a concern.
